text: The Digaro (Digarish), Northern Mishmi (Mishmic), or Kera'a–Tawrã languages are a possible small family of possibly Sino-Tibetan languages spoken by the Mishmi people of southeastern Tibet and Arunachal Pradesh.

title: Digaro Mishmi language and alphabet
text: Digaro Mishmi belongs to the Central Tibeto-Burman branch of the Sino-Tibetan language family. It is spoken by about 45,000 people mainly in northeast of India in the Lohit district of Arunachal Pradesh, and in the Dibang Valley district of Assam.
